items: **API** (`api`, items-core's `@bw/gateway`): the console API and the consumer API (by `Host`), schedule firing, the sweep and `run_events` partition upkeep, in one always-on container. Its migrations run as a job before each deploy.

**Worker and browser** (`worker`, `browser`): one direct worker, `gw-1`, reaching Chrome over CDP by the browser's service name on the stack's network.

**Workers connect to Postgres directly**, as the restricted `aitems_worker` role, which a job makes before each deploy. They hold no token, have no API URL, listen for no inbound traffic and run no DDL. A worker joins the fleet the first time it starts, under its `WORKER_NAME`.

**Data**: the gateway's shared Postgres (a database and owner role for the stack, dumped each night); page content and screenshots on volumes, the content one shared by the API and the worker; workflow blobs in Postgres.
**Addresses** through the gateway's Caddy, on the LAN and over Tailscale only.
Remote machines provide browsers or proxies only (the plan's rule).

intro: A ticket marked `byYou` is yours: the live gateway, an external account, credentials, or a go/no-go. The others can be written (code or docs) for your review.

items: **One transport.** No HTTP worker ever reaches the gateway's database. There is no fallback and no transport switch.
**Workers never run DDL.** The API creates the weekly partitions. A worker refuses to boot without next week's, and stops claiming while any of the coming seven days is uncovered.

**Leases are fenced by epoch.** A killed worker hands nothing back: its leases lapse after 30 seconds and a new boot reclaims the runs from the durable log. A worker whose lease was taken over has its writes refused.

**The shared Postgres is every stack's.** By the cloud budget's terms items-core takes up to 44 connections while its API rolls out, operators' reserve included, and a second worker adds 10; IC-20.1 measures what the other stacks leave.
**A stop is sticky.** A stopped worker exits again on every start until its fleet row is deleted. `restart: on-failure` leaves it down, and a deploy fails its check meanwhile.
**`NOLOGIN` doesn't end live sessions.** To cut a worker off at the database, also `pg_terminate_backend` its `items-worker:<bootId>` sessions.
**Storage settings must match** on the API and the worker: `STORAGE_PROVIDER`, `CONTENT_STORAGE_DIR` on the volume they share, and `WORKFLOW_BLOB_STORAGE_PROVIDER`.
**The clock check stays at 5 s.** Fix a drifting clock rather than setting `WORKER_ALLOW_UNSAFE_CLOCK_SKEW`, and never use that in an acceptance run.
**The worker fetches from the gateway machine's internet address**, your home connection: a real site's block lands there.
**A push to items-core's `main` deploys everything on it** once the stack exists.

plan.title: Add the stack's compose file with the API, console, worker and browser services
plan.description:
`deploy/compose.yaml`, the stack's compose text, with four services. None publishes a port: Caddy reaches the API and the console through the stack's Caddy connection (IC-18.2).

- **`api`**, items-core's API (`@bw/gateway`, `docker/gateway/Dockerfile`), not named `gateway`, which on this machine is the gateway's own stack. Postgres from the stack's shared-Postgres connection, renamed by interpolation (`POSTGRES_HOST: ${GW_api__PGHOST}`, and so on for the port, database, user and password). `API_HOST=0.0.0.0`, port 3000, `LOG_FORMAT=json`, `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `GATEWAY_CONSUMER_HOSTS=items-api.bendelhome.cc` (the consumer API's address, by your answer on IC-18), and `AI_PROVIDER` and `AI_API_KEY` as placeholders, since boot requires them and nothing reads them. `init: true`, and `order: start-first` so the console keeps answering through a deploy (two containers at once, as Cloud Run's rollouts had, which the connection budget counts). Its healthcheck asks the partitions endpoint with Node's `fetch` (the image has no curl), by your answer on alerts.
- **`console`**, `docker/web/Dockerfile` with its production `build` (no sign-in bypass), `API_UPSTREAM=http://api:3000`, a healthcheck with busybox `wget`.
- **`worker`**, `docker/worker/Dockerfile`: `WORKER_NAME=gw-1`, `WORKER_CONCURRENCY=4` (the cloud plan's), `BROWSER_CDP_HOST=browser`, `BROWSER_CDP_PORT=9222`. The Postgres host, port and database come from the API's connection variables by interpolation, but it connects as `aitems_worker` with a password of its own, made by the gateway, never the owner's. `init: true`; `restart: on-failure`, so a stop from the fleet page (exit 0) leaves it down while a crash (exit 1) restarts it; `order: stop-first`, since two containers under one `WORKER_NAME` evict each other. No healthcheck: it listens on nothing, a deploy watches it for 10 s, and the fleet page shows its presence beat.
- **`browser`**, `docker/browser/Dockerfile`'s `prod` target with `PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION=1.63.0`, `shm_size: 2gb`, a healthcheck with `curl` on `/json/version`. The worker reaches it at `browser:9222` on the stack's own network.

Storage: `STORAGE_PROVIDER=local` and `WORKFLOW_BLOB_STORAGE_PROVIDER=postgres` on both the API and the worker, page content on one named volume both mount at the same `CONTENT_STORAGE_DIR` (the API reads what the worker writes), screenshots on the API's own volume, and no bucket (the storage part of IC-6.6). The sweep endpoint stays closed (`WORKFLOW_SWEEP_TOKEN` unset): Cloud Scheduler backed up an instance Cloud Run could idle, and here the API's container is always on, so its in-process sweep and hourly partition upkeep run.

plan.title: Add the `migrate`, `worker-role`, `seed` and `seed-workflows` jobs to the stack's compose file
plan.description:
Four one-off jobs in `deploy/compose.yaml`, the first two run before each deploy, in this order:

- **`migrate`** (`profiles: [job, before-deploy]`): the API's image running `pnpm --filter @bw/cli db:migrate:all` as the database's owner role. It also seeds the `run_events` partitions, without which a worker refuses to boot.
- **`worker-role`** (`profiles: [job, before-deploy]`): `postgres:18.4` running `docs/workflow/worker-role.sql` (the repository's `docs/workflow` mounted read-only) as the owner role, with the worker's password, so `aitems_worker` exists with its grants before the worker starts, and a new password reaches the role before the worker uses it. It is safe to run again (`CREATE` or `ALTER ROLE`). The owner role needs `may_create: roles` on the Postgres connection, which since Postgres 16 reaches only the roles it made; the worker's probe, which refuses a role that is a member of another, is unaffected, since the owner is a member of `aitems_worker`, not the other way round. The password is made once, as the worker's variable, and read here by interpolation.
- **`seed`** (`profiles: [job]`): the API's image running the structural seeds (`apps/gateway/src/cli/seed.ts`, no fakes): the sites, merchants and brands, and the workflow definitions. It empties every table it seeds first, so it runs once, on the new database (IC-18.5).
- **`seed-workflows`** (`profiles: [job]`): the API's image running `seed-workflow-engine.ts`, which only inserts missing workflow definitions and versions; run after a graph changes (the cloud runbook's step 5).

Done 2026-10-16 (`e0b99793`). `worker-role` takes the password from its environment (`WORKER_PASSWORD`, from `${GW_worker__POSTGRES_PASS}`) through psql's `getenv`, so it is on no command line; `worker-role.sql` is unchanged. A second run changes the password and the old one is refused. `seed` and `seed-workflows` run `node --import tsx` directly, since the package scripts need a dotenv file. All four jobs exit 0 on a new database.
